UPDATE: In response to the clinic's reply
Your response does not accurately reflect my experience.
Your email explicitly stated: “Pre-visit sedative oral medication". You now describe this as medication intended to “help reduce your cat’s anxiety.” Those are not the same descriptions. I relied on that wording when deciding to pay for the medication.
I had also informed your clinic that my cat is not easy to handle, both in writing and verbally. The fact that I described my cat as difficult to handle should have prompted you to clarify whether I would be able to administer oral medication to her. When I expressed surprise and concern about receiving pills, your receptionist did not offer liquid gabapentin. Instead, she gave me a Catit Creamy treat and assured me I could mix the pill with it and that it will work. If, as you now claim, I was offered liquid gabapentin as an alternative, why would I have refused it when I was clearly surprised and concerned about receiving pills in the first place? I did not refuse such an offer because no such offer was made to me.
I will be sending you a formal demand letter by registered mail regarding this matter. I will proceed accordingly after you receive it.

I contacted the clinic about my sick, older cat. I explained that she becomes extremely stressed and asked whether she could be sedated to make the process easier and less stressful for both her and the veterinary staff. I was told in writing that she would receive pre-visit sedative oral medication, costing $40.88.
Based on that information, my understanding was that I would be receiving a sedative medication.
When I went to the clinic to pick up the medication, the receptionist gave me a pre-prepared package and charged me $40.88. After I had paid, I noticed that I had been given gabapentin and trazodone.
My understanding is that gabapentin and trazodone are not sedative medications. They are Calming medications and they have no effect on my cat.
This was the first point at which I felt that the information I had been given was misleading. I had specifically asked about sedation and I was told in writing that is what I will receive but I was given calming medications instead.
At that point, I was already extremely overwhelmed. I had been dealing with my cat's health problems for about a month and was very worried about her. I became very upset and left the clinic because I did not want to react in a way that I might regret later.
I was frustrated because I knew there was no realistic way for me to give my cat pills safely. I had already communicated my concerns about this to the clinic, but I felt that those concerns had been disregarded.
Nevertheless, that night I attempted to give her the medication. I struggled for approximately an hour, was injured in the process, and my cat experienced significant stress.
I then emailed the clinic to explain what had happened and express my frustration. In response, I was told that I had been given the option of liquid or pills and that I had chosen pills.
That is not what happened. I was never offered a choice between liquid and pills. I can’t even comprehend how easily they can lie. It is beyond my imagination. Be kind to yourself and your loved ones, and take your pets somewhere else. If they could lie that easily over $40, just imagine how far they might go to get access to your wallet at your pet’s expense.
I requested a refund, but the clinic refused.
I am asking for my money to be refunded. At this point, it is much less about the $40.88 than it is about accountability, transparency, and honesty. I believe that a veterinary clinic should communicate clearly with pet owners and accurately represent what medication is being provided, especially when an owner is already dealing with a sick and highly stressed animal.  I have already sent a formal complaint to OMVQ.
Thank you for the review! :)

I had a very disappointing experience with this veterinary clinic.

I initially booked an appointment for my dog for a general check-up, surgery, vaccinations, and microchipping. I specifically requested to have all procedures done on the same day. However, I was not properly informed about how the appointment would be handled. During the first visit, they only administered the vaccines and asked me to pay for them separately. Then, when I arrived in person, I was charged an additional consultation fee that was twice as high as expected, without any prior warning.

Moreover, the microchipping and surgery were not done at all. I was simply told to book another appointment. I did so and returned with my dog for the scheduled surgery.

What happened next was extremely concerning. The staff put my dog under anesthesia without conducting a proper preliminary examination. Only after that did they notice some spots on her skin and claimed it could be ringworm. Later, it turned out that it was not ringworm at all.

As a result, I was charged extra for unnecessary tests, anesthesia, and a catheter — all due to the clinic’s negligence in not examining my dog beforehand. On top of that, they prescribed medications that were completely unnecessary. I followed their instructions and treated my dog, only to later find out that she was perfectly healthy and did not need any treatment at all.

Overall, this experience caused unnecessary stress for both me and my dog, as well as significant extra expenses. I cannot recommend this clinic due to the lack of professionalism, poor communication, and questionable medical practices.

I am writing this as a warning to other pet owners who value transparency and professional integrity. I have been a high-volume client at this clinic, recently spending thousands for the care of my six animals. While Dr. Lissa has shown compassion in the past, the current administrative management under Samantha has made this practice a liability to my animals' health.
Specifically, after a clinical 'green light' was given by the veterinarian on March 9th, the clinic manager, Samantha, weaponized the OMVQ '20-day' rule to stall the release of my own pet’s medical records. Withholding essential lab data for a pending surgical consultation is a direct breach of the continuity of care and is clinically irresponsible.
The manager’s argumentative and controlling conduct has forced me to immediately terminate the care for all six of my animals and move them to a practice that respects both the owner and the medical timeline. If you require efficiency, honesty, or timely access to the records you have paid for, I strongly suggest looking elsewhere. Integrity is non-negotiable when lives are at stake.

I’ve taken my dog to this clinic on and off for a few years, and I’m sure they are a great clinic for many people, but ultimately they weren’t the right fit for me.

During my most recent visit in December, the appointment felt very rushed — it was scheduled for an hour but the appointment lasted 15 minutes and I didn’t feel the vet took the time to properly examine my dog or fully address my concerns. Because my dog was being difficult, a technician was brought in to help hold her, but it didn’t seem to lead to a more thorough exam. The overall tone felt hurried, which left me feeling uneasy.

At checkout, I was told I would receive a call to schedule a surgery in January, but it’s now February and I never heard back. The lack of follow-up reinforced my concerns about communication and attention to detail.

Given the experience, I decided to return to my original vet for a second opinion. I truly wish the team well, but for my dog’s care I’ll be going elsewhere.
